resources.title: Physics formulae
resources.content:
### Electricity

| Quantity | Equation |
|---|---|
| Potential difference | $V = IR$ |
| Power | $P = IV = I^{2}R = \dfrac{V^{2}}{R}$ |
| Resistors in series | $R_\text{total} = R_1 + R_2 + \dots$ |
| Resistors in parallel | $\dfrac{1}{R_\text{total}} = \dfrac{1}{R_1} + \dfrac{1}{R_2} + \dots$ |
| Charge | $Q = It$ |

### Motion and energy

| Quantity | Equation |
|---|---|
| Speed | $v = \dfrac{d}{t}$ |
| Acceleration | $a = \dfrac{v - u}{t}$ |
| Equation of motion | $v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as$ |
| Kinetic energy | $E_\text{k} = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^{2}$ |
| Gravitational potential energy | $E_\text{p} = mgh$ |

Gravitational field strength $g = 9.8\ \text{N kg}^{-1}$

questions.context: Magnesium ribbon reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid. Bubbles of a colourless gas are produced and the magnesium disappears.
questions.text: Write the balanced symbol equation, **including state symbols**, for this reaction.
questions.markScheme:
$\ce{Mg(s) + 2HCl(aq) -> MgCl2(aq) + H2(g)}$
- correct formulae of all reactants and products [1]
- balanced **and** correct state symbols [1]

questions.context: Sodium hydroxide solution is added to a solution containing iron(III) ions, $\ce{Fe^{3+}}$. An orange-brown precipitate forms (Figure 1).

images.alt: Test tube containing an orange-brown precipitate at the bottom
images.caption: Figure 1: the precipitate formed

questions.text: Write the ionic equation, with state symbols, for the formation of the precipitate.
questions.markScheme:
$\ce{Fe^{3+}(aq) + 3OH^-(aq) -> Fe(OH)3(s)}$
- correct ions and product [1]
- balanced charges **and** state symbols [1]

questions.context:
Ethanoic acid is a weak acid. In water it is only partly ionised:

$$\ce{CH3COOH(aq) <=> CH3COO^-(aq) + H+(aq)}$$
questions.text: Solid sodium ethanoate, $\ce{CH3COONa}$, is dissolved in the solution. Explain what happens to the position of equilibrium **and** to the pH.
questions.markScheme:
- sodium ethanoate adds $\ce{CH3COO-}$ ions, increasing their concentration [1]
- position of equilibrium shifts to the **left** (Le Chatelier's principle) [1]
- $[\ce{H+}]$ decreases, so the pH **increases** [1]

For reference (not required): $$K_a = \frac{[\ce{CH3COO-}][\ce{H+}]}{[\ce{CH3COOH}]}$$

questions.text: Identify the correct formula of ammonium sulfate.
questions.markScheme: **B**: $\ce{(NH4)2SO4}$. Two $\ce{NH4+}$ ions balance the charge of one $\ce{SO4^{2-}}$ ion. [1]

questions.context: The cell in Figure 2 has an emf $\varepsilon = 6.0\ \text{V}$ and negligible internal resistance. $R_1 = 4.0\ \Omega$ and $R_2 = 8.0\ \Omega$.
questions.imageAlt: Series circuit with a cell, resistors R1 and R2, an ammeter and a voltmeter connected across R2
questions.text: Calculate the reading on the ammeter **and** the power dissipated in $R_2$. Use $V = IR$ and $P = I^{2}R$.
questions.markScheme:
- $R_\text{total} = R_1 + R_2 = 4.0 + 8.0 = 12\ \Omega$ [1]
- $I = \dfrac{\varepsilon}{R_\text{total}} = \dfrac{6.0}{12} = 0.50\ \text{A}$ [1]
- $P = I^{2}R_2 = (0.50)^{2} \times 8.0$ [1]
- $P = 2.0\ \text{W}$ [1]

Allow error carried forward from an incorrect current.

questions.context: A ball of mass $m = 0.20\ \text{kg}$ is dropped from rest from a height $h = 5.0\ \text{m}$. Air resistance is negligible and $g = 9.81\ \text{m s}^{-2}$. While it falls, $\vec{F}_\text{net} = m\vec{g}$.
questions.text: Show that the speed of the ball just before it hits the ground is given by $v = \sqrt{2gh}$, and calculate this speed.
questions.markScheme:
$$mgh = \tfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} \quad\Rightarrow\quad v = \sqrt{2gh}$$
- equates gravitational potential energy lost to kinetic energy gained [1]
- $v = \sqrt{2 \times 9.81 \times 5.0}$ [1]
- $v = 9.90\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ (accept 9.9) [1]

questions.context:
A student added marble chips to excess dilute hydrochloric acid and measured the volume of carbon dioxide collected:

$$\ce{CaCO3(s) + 2HCl(aq) -> CaCl2(aq) + H2O(l) + CO2(g)}$$
questions.text: Calculate the mean rate of reaction in the first 30 s, in cm$^{3}$ s$^{-1}$.
Describe the trend in the data **and** explain it using collision theory.
questions.markScheme:
| Marking point | Mark |
|---|:---:|
| Rate is fastest at the start / volume rises quickly at first | [1] |
| Rate decreases as the acid and marble are used up: fewer collisions per second | [1] |
| Reaction stops at 60 cm$^{3}$ (180 s) when the limiting reactant ($\ce{CaCO3}$) is used up | [1] |

Expected shape of the graph:

markSchemeImages.alt: Graph of volume of CO2 against time rising steeply then levelling off at 60 cm3
markSchemeImages.caption: Volume of $\ce{CO2}$ against time
